# Generated failures and endpoint classes point back to the Phrase source
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #161, sha256:fc504526090878adc991d0d64afa41749fe9b302d2196501415b0c2706364b1c). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; from the Usable v1 retro product feedback)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Product feedback gathered from Codex and Grok at the Usable v1 retro, 2026-10-28 (docs/retros/usable-v1-2026-10-28.md): the demo's real rules, validation, storing and updating, all sit in native C#, so a cold model has to learn generated C# conventions to change them and a reader of the Phrase cannot see the rule.
- **Depends on:** 138
- **Story:** As Morgan, I want a production failure in the generated API to name the Phrase endpoint, step and failure it came from, so that I can trace it back to the spec without reading generated C#.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a generated endpoint, When it fails with a declared failure, Then the 422 body or the log line names the Phrase file, the endpoint and the failure name, and a unit test asserts it for every failure of the Tasks demo
  2. Given generated C#, When it is read, Then each generated file and method carries a short comment with the Phrase source location (file and line of the endpoint or phrase), and the comment is stable across rebuilds of an unchanged source
  3. Given the specs, When the traceability lands, Then no spec changes and the response body shape the specs assert is unchanged (the detail goes in a header or log, not the declared fields) unless a Decider says otherwise

## Context

- A reader the personas may miss: the engineer on call who must trace a production failure back through generated code (found at the Usable v1 retro). Prefer the smallest change that makes the trace possible.
